questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical NLP extraction skills under real-world constraints typical of job platforms.

## Key Concepts
- Multilingual information extraction from user-generated content
- Tiny on-device models, inference optimization, and quantization techniques
- Code-switching handling, data labeling workflows, and privacy-by-design architecture

## Code Example
```javascript
function extractJob(posting) {
  const title = (posting.split('title:')[1] || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
  const location = (posting.split('location:')[1] || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
  const skills = (posting.split('skills:')[1] || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
  const remote = /remote|home.?office|telecommut/i.test(posting);
  const seniority = /senior|junior|lead|manager|intern/i.test(posting) ? 
    posting.match(/senior|junior|lead|manager|intern/i)[0] : 'mid';
  
  return { title, location, skills, remote, seniority };
}
```

## Labeling Plan
- Use heuristic-labeled data from structured job feeds as initial training data
- Apply human-in-the-loop validation for ambiguous cases
- Implement confidence thresholds to route low-confidence extractions to rules or human review

## Latency & Privacy
- On-device inference ensures <100 ms latency with quantized TinyBERT
- No data leaves the device, satisfying privacy requirements

## Offline Evaluation
- Test on held-out multilingual dataset covering all three languages and code-switching scenarios
- Measure precision/recall per field and overall schema completeness

## Staged Rollout
- Phase 1: Rule-based extraction only (baseline)
- Phase 2: Hybrid model + rules on 5% of traffic
- Phase 3: Full rollout with A/B testing and monitoring

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design practical, on-device NLP systems under strict size, latency, and privacy constraints.

## Key Concepts

- On-device ML and model compression (quantization, pruning)
- Lexicon-based normalization with fallback to tiny classifiers
- Multilingual embeddings and cross-lingual transfer learning
- Entity normalization to canonical IDs via post-processing
- Privacy-by-design, offline evaluation, and staged rollout strategy

## Code Example

```python
# Pseudo-logic for on-device detection + mapping
def detect_and_normalize(text, model, lexicon):
    spans = model.detect_entities(text)
    results = []
    for span in spans:
        canonical_id = lexicon.lookup(span.text)
        if canonical_id is None:
            canonical_id = model.classify(span.text)
        results.append({'span': span, 'product_id': canonical_id})
    return results
```

```python
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# Inference with latency check
import time
def predict_hate_speech(text):
    start = time.time()
    normalized = normalize_transliteration(text)
    features = vectorizer.transform([normalized])
    prediction = clf.predict(features)[0]
    latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000
    return prediction, latency < 200
```

- **Privacy**: Process locally without data transmission to external services

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to build privacy-preserving, low-latency NLP systems for code-switched language (EN/HI) with bias detection, remediation, and governance in enterprise chat environments.

## Key Concepts

- On-device processing for latency and privacy compliance
- Code-switch handling with EN/HI bilingual resources
- Hybrid detection combining lexicon-based rules with a contextual encoder
- Remediation module providing explainable rewrite suggestions
- Drift-aware evaluation and staged rollout with rollback plans

## Implementation Approach

The system employs a two-tier detection strategy. The on-device tier uses a compact bilingual lexicon paired with a lightweight contextual encoder to achieve sub-100ms latency while preserving privacy by processing sensitive data locally. For ambiguous cases, cloud inference leverages a distilled multilingual model to improve accuracy. The remediation module generates neutral rewrite suggestions with confidence scores, enabling users to self-correct flagged content. High-severity cases automatically escalate to compliance review via the governance gate. Continuous drift-aware evaluation monitors model performance, triggering automated rollback if latency or accuracy degrades beyond defined thresholds.
